statements.claim: The women had left their husbands' great sacrifice, carried food through the forest, and fed Krishna and his cowherd companions with their own hands.
statements.evidence: Preceding event in the arc (SB 10.23.1-19, prev story DKS_0095 'The Brahmanas' Wives Bring Food to Krishna'); DKS_0097's pack confirms the wives 'had gone instead, carrying food through the woods' and SB 10.23.35: 'bhagavān api govindas tenaivānnena gopakān' — Govinda fed the cowherd boys with that very food.

statements.claim: They stood before him in a grove on the banks of the Yamuna, where the ashoka trees were tipped with fresh young leaves.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.20: 'yamunopavane 'śoka nava-pallava-maṇḍite' — in the Yamuna pleasure-grove adorned with ashoka trees in fresh leaf.

statements.claim: They had known him before they ever saw him — their hearts already sunk in him, their ears filled with the nectar of hearing about him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.22: 'prāyaḥ-śruta-priyatamodaya-karṇa-pūrair yasmin nimagna-manasas' — minds immersed in him through hearing of the dearest one.

statements.claim: Krishna stood like a dancer at ease — one hand on a companion's shoulder, the other twirling a lotus, dark skin, gold garments, forest-flower garland, peacock feather, earrings, lotus-bright smiling face.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.21: 'śyāmaṃ hiraṇya-paridhiṃ vanamālya-barha-dhātu-pravāla-naṭa-veṣam anavratāṃse vinyasta-hastam itareṇa dhunānam abjaṃ karṇotpalālaka-kapola-mukhābja-hāsam' — dark, gold-clad, forest garland and peacock feather, dancer's garb, hand on a companion's shoulder, twirling a lotus with the other, earrings at cheeks, lotus-face with a smile.

statements.claim: The women drank him in through their eyes, and the sorrow that had followed them from home left them, the way the wise give up their false ideas of self.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.22: 'antaḥ praveśya su-ciraṃ parirabhya tāpaṃ prājñaṃ yathābhimatayo vijahur' — taking him in through the eyes, they abandoned their sorrow as the wise abandon their misconceptions.

statements.claim: Krishna said: "You are welcome. Sit. Tell me what I can do for you."
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.24: 'svāgataṃ vo mahā-bhāgā āsyatāṃ karavāma kim'.

statements.claim: The wise see what is best for themselves and give him all they have — breath, mind, intelligence, wife, children, wealth.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.25-26: 'nanv addhā mayi kurvanti kuśalāḥ svārtha-darśinaḥ / prāṇa-buddhi-manaḥ-svātma dārāpatya-dhanādayaḥ'.

statements.claim: He told them to return to the place of sacrifice, since their husbands were brahmanas.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.27: 'tad yāta deva-yajanaṃ patayo vo dvijātayaḥ'.

statements.claim: The women answered: "Do not speak such cruel words. We have left everyone — fathers, husbands, sons, brothers — so that we might carry on our heads the tulasi garland fallen from your feet. Neither they nor any stranger will take us back; for us who have fallen at your feet there is no other refuge. Grant us this."
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.28-29: 'maivaṃ vibho 'rhati bhavān gadituṃ nṛ-śaṃsaṃ ... prāptā vayaṃ tulasi-dāma padāvasṛṣṭaṃ keśair nivoḍhum atilaṅghya samasta-bandhūn / gṛhṇanti no na patayaḥ pitarau sutā vā na bhrātṛ-bandhu-suhṛdaḥ kuta eva cānye tasmād bhavat-prapadayoḥ patitātmanāṃ no nānyā bhaved gatir ... tad vidhehi'.

statements.claim: Krishna was pleased and granted them the grace they asked, teaching that he is won by remembrance — hearing, seeing, holding him in the mind, speaking of him — not by bodily nearness, and sent them home with hearts fixed on him.
statements.evidence: Index summary: 'Krishna, pleased with their devotion, assures them of his grace and sends them back with their minds fixed on him'; pack excerpt: 'teaching that he is won by remembrance rather than by nearness'; SB 10.23.31 + 10.23.32: 'na prītaye 'nurāgāya hy aṅga-saṅgo ... / śravaṇād darśanād dhyānān mayi bhāvo 'nukīrtanāt'.

notes: All plot points map directly to SB 10.23.20-31; the food-carrying opening is the established preceding event (10.23.1-19, DKS_0095).

statements.claim: The sacrifice had the right place, hour, offerings, mantras, and fires tended by priests who knew every rule.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.47 (the brahmanas' own enumeration): 'deśaḥ kālaḥ pṛthag dravyaṃ mantra-tantrartvijo 'gnayaḥ'.

statements.claim: When a young cowherd came asking for food, sent by his companion Krishna who waited hungry in the forest with his friends, they waved him away.
statements.evidence: Established preceding event (SB 10.23.1-19, prev story DKS_0095); pack excerpt: 'the Lord they had spurned'; SB 10.23.8/11: they did not heed the request.

statements.claim: It was their wives who had gone instead, carrying food through the woods to Krishna and his friends, and Krishna fed the cowherds with that very food.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.35: 'bhagavān api govindas tenaivānnena gopakān' — Govinda fed the cowherds with that same food.

statements.claim: Even the one wife whose husband had held her back by force was not stopped; she closed her eyes and went to Krishna in her mind, meditating on the Lord as she had heard of him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.34: 'tatraikā vidhṛtā bhartrā bhagavantaṃ yathā-śrutam' — one held back by her husband [meditated on] the Lord as she had heard; cf. 10.23.32 'śravaṇād darśanād dhyānāt'.

statements.claim: The one they had refused was Vishnu himself — the Lord standing in the forest in the shape of a cowherd boy.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.48: 'sa eva bhagavān sākṣād viṣṇur yogeśvareśvaraḥ'; 10.23.36: 'līlā-nara-vapur nr-lokam anuśīlayan' — playing a human form.

statements.claim: "Shame on our birth, and on its threefold aims. Shame on our vows. Shame on our great learning."
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.39: 'dhig janma nas tri-vṛd yat tad dhig vrataṃ dhig bahu-jñatām'.

statements.claim: The Lord's power to delude could bewilder even the wise, even the yogis.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.40: 'nūnaṃ bhagavato māyā yoginām api mohinī'.

statements.claim: The women had no initiation into the brahminical way and no long years of study in a guru's house, yet they loved Krishna, the teacher of all the worlds, with a love that shamed the men's learning.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.41-43: 'aho paśyata nārīṇām api kṛṣṇe jagad-gurau / nāsāṃ dvijāti-saṃskāro na nivāso gurāv api / tathāpi hy uttamaḥ-śloke kṛṣṇe yogeśvareśvare'.

statements.claim: The place, the hour, the separate offerings, the mantras, the priests, the fires — all were Krishna himself; he is whom the goddess of fortune serves, ever longing for the touch of his feet; he needs nothing yet grants liberation.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.45-48: 'anyathā pūrṇa-kāmasya kaivalyādy-aśiṣāṃ pateḥ / hitvānyān bhajate yaṃ śrīḥ pāda-sparśāśayāsakṛt / deśaḥ kālaḥ pṛthag dravyaṃ mantra-tantrartvijo 'gnayaḥ / sa eva bhagavān sākṣād viṣṇur yogeśvareśvaraḥ'.

statements.claim: "Salutations to the Lord Krishna, whose wisdom never falters. He is Vishnu himself, the lord of all lords of yoga, the first being of all — and it is his own power that keeps our minds deluded."
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.49-50: 'tasmai namo bhagavate kṛṣṇāyākuṇṭha-medhase / sa vai na ādyaḥ puruṣaḥ sva-māyā-mohitātmanām'.

statements.claim: They remembered their fault and the insult they had offered him, and longed to see him — but they did not go, because Kamsa ruled nearby and they were afraid.
statements.evidence: SB 10.23.51: 'iti svāgham anusmṛtya kṛṣṇe te kṛta-helanāḥ'; pack excerpt: 'yearn for his sight yet do not dare approach, fearing Kamsa'.

notes: All claims map to SB 10.23.32-51; the cowherd-refusal opening is the established preceding event (10.23.1-19, DKS_0095).

statements.claim: The moon rose full over Vrindavan, painting the sky with red light.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.1-2: 'tadoḍurājaḥ kakubhaḥ karair mukhaṃ prācyā vilimpann aruṇena' — the moon tinting the directions with red rays; 'akhaṇḍa-maṇḍalaṃ ... nava-kuṅkumāruṇam' — full disc, red like fresh kumkum.

statements.claim: When Krishna's flute sounded, the women of Vraja heard it amid their ordinary tasks and set them down — one left milking, another left milk half-boiled over the fire, another turned from a husband she was serving, another from a child she was feeding.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.3-6: 'niśamya gītāṃ ... vraja-striyaḥ kṛṣṇa-gṛhīta-mānasāḥ ... duhantyo 'bhiyayuḥ kāścid dohaṃ hitvā ... payo 'dhiśritya ... pariveṣayantyas tad dhitvā pāyayantyaḥ śiśūn payaḥ śuśrūṣantyaḥ patīn kāścid aśnantyo 'pāsya bhojanam'.

statements.claim: Some came with their clothes and ornaments half arranged, so great was their haste.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.6: 'vyatyasta-vastrābharaṇāḥ kāścit kṛṣṇāntikaṃ yayuḥ' — some went to Krishna with clothes and ornaments askew.

statements.claim: Some who were shut inside their houses stood where they were, closed their eyes, and held him in their minds.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.8: 'antar-gṛha-gatāḥ kāścid gopyo 'labdha-vinirgamāḥ kṛṣṇaṃ tad-bhāvanā-yuktā dadhyur mīlita-locanāḥ'.

statements.claim: Their families called them back, but they did not turn — Krishna had taken their minds, and they went where the music led.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.7: 'tā vāryamāṇāḥ patibhiḥ pitṛbhir bhrātṛ-bandhubhiḥ govindāpahṛtātmāno na nyavartanta mohitāḥ'.

statements.claim: Pride rose in the gopis out of their good fortune — the sense that they, of all people, possessed him.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (SB 10.29.47): 'Seeing the pride that had arisen in the gopis from their good fortune'.

statements.claim: Where he had been, there was nothing — he vanished then and there, in the middle of the night, in the middle of their happiness.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (SB 10.29.47): 'Krishna vanished then and there'.

statements.claim: He did not leave them to punish them but to humble them, and to favor them.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (SB 10.29.47): 'to humble them and favor them'.

statements.claim: The flute had stopped; the place where he had stood still held his warmth, and the gopis stood speechless in the red moonlight.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric aftermath of the vanishing (10.29.47); no pack statement on the flute or the gopis' posture after the disappearance, contradicts nothing.

statements.claim: The moon had not dimmed and the forest had not changed; only he was gone.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric close consistent with 10.30.1-3 (the gopis left searching), no factual assertion needing source.

notes: Core claims (moon, flute summons, house-bound gopis, pride, vanishing, motive) map to SB 10.29.1-8, 47.

statements.claim: When the gopis finally reached Krishna that autumn night, he greeted them with a smile and a question: "You are welcome. What can I do for you? Is all well in Vraja? Tell me why you have come."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.17-18: 'svāgataṃ vo mahā-bhāgāḥ priyaṃ kiṃ karavāṇi vaḥ / vrajasyānāmayaṃ kaccid brūtāgamana-kāraṇam'. The 'autumn night' setting is traditional rasa-lila framing not stated in the pack passage (see notes).

statements.claim: "This night is fearsome, and full of fierce creatures. It is not right for women to be here. Go back to Vraja."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.18: 'rajany eṣā ghora-rūpā ghora-sattva-niṣevitā / pratiyāta vrajaṃ neha stheyaṃ strībhiḥ'.

statements.claim: "Your mothers and fathers, your sons and brothers and husbands, are searching for you, and they cannot find you. Do not bring such distress on your own family."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.19: 'mātaraḥ pitaraḥ putrā bhrātaraḥ patayaś ca vaḥ / vicinvanti hy apaśyanto mā kṛḍhvaṃ bandhu-sādhvasam'.

statements.claim: He pointed to the forest — the flowering trees lit by the full moon, the Yamuna's breeze moving through the leaves.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.20: 'dṛṣṭaṃ vanaṃ kusumitaṃ rākeśa-kara-rañjitam / yamunānila-līlaijat taru-pallava-śobhitam'.

statements.claim: "Return to the settlement without delay. Serve your husbands. The calves and the little ones are crying; go milk the cows and feed them."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.21: 'tad yāta mā ciraṃ goṣṭhaṃ śuśrūṣadhvaṃ patīn satīḥ / krandanti vatsā bālāś ca tān pāyayata duhyata'.

statements.claim: "If it is love for me that has bound your hearts and brought you here, that is only fitting — for every living thing finds its joy in me."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.22: 'atha vā mad-abhisnehād bhavatyo yantritāśayāḥ / āgatā hy upapannaṃ vaḥ prīyante mayi jantavaḥ'.

statements.claim: "The highest duty of a woman is to serve her husband faithfully, to do good to her own people, and to care for those who depend on her."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.23: 'bhartuḥ śuśrūṣaṇaṃ strīṇāṃ paro dharmo hy amāyayā / tad-bandhūnāṃ ca kalyāṇaḥ prajānāṃ cānupoṣaṇam'.

statements.claim: "A wife must not leave her husband — not even one who is ill-tempered, or unlucky, or old, or dull, or sick, or poor."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.24: 'duḥśīlo durbhago vṛddho jaḍo rogy adhano 'pi vā / patiḥ strībhir na hātavyo lokepsubhir apātakī'.

statements.claim: "A love outside marriage brings no heaven and no honor; it is trifling and painful and feared, and it disgraces a woman of good family."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.25: 'asvargyam ayaśasyaṃ ca phalgu kṛcchraṃ bhayāvaham / jugupsitaṃ ca sarvatra hy aupapatyaṃ kula-striyaḥ'.

statements.claim: "Love for me is born of hearing about me, and seeing me, and meditating on me, and speaking of me. It is not born of standing near me."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.26: 'śravaṇād darśanād dhyānān mayi bhāvo 'nukīrtanāt / na tathā sannikarṣeṇa pratiyāta tato gṛhān'.

statements.claim: Their hopes broke, a grief they could not cross settled over them; they stood with faces turned down, lips dried with sighing, tracing lines in the earth with their toes, wiping away tears that streaked the vermilion on their chests, saying nothing.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.27-28: 'viṣaṇṇā bhagna-saṅkalpāś cintām āpur duratyayām / kṛtvā mukhāny ava śucaḥ śvasanena śuṣyad bimbādharāṇi caraṇena bhuvaḥ likhantyaḥ / asrair upātta-masibhiḥ kuca-kuṅkumāni tasthur mṛjantya uru-duḥkha-bharāḥ sma tūṣṇīm'.

statements.claim: One of them answered: "Do not speak such cruel words. We have left behind every pleasure we had, and come to your feet. Accept us, your own devotees. Do not cast us off — the way the ancient Lord receives those who long for freedom."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.31: 'maivaṃ vibho 'rhati bhavān gadituṃ nṛ-śaṃsaṃ santyajya sarva-viṣayāṃs tava pāda-mūlam / bhaktā bhajasva duravagraha mā tyajāsmān devo yathādi-puruṣo bhajate mumukṣūn'.

statements.claim: "You, who understand duty, have told us that a woman's dharma is to serve her husband and her children and her people. Let it be so. But you are the dearest of all who have bodies; you are our friend, our very self. Of what use to us are husbands and sons, who bring only sorrow? Do not cut down the hope we have carried for you so long, O lotus-eyed one."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.32: 'yat paty-apatya-suhṛdām anuvṛttir aṅga strīṇāṃ sva-dharma iti dharma-vidā tvayoktam / astv evam etad ... preṣṭho bhavāṃs tanu-bhṛtāṃ kila bandhur ātmā ... nitya-priye pati-sutādibhir ārti-daiḥ kim ... mā sma chindyā āśāṃ dhṛtāṃ tvayi cirād aravinda-netra'.

statements.claim: "Our minds have been carried away by you; they cannot go back into our houses. Our hands no longer do the work of the house, and our feet will not move from the foot of your feet. How shall we go back to Vraja? What would we do there?"
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.33: 'cittaṃ sukhena bhavatāpahṛtaṃ gṛheṣu yan nirviśaty uta karāv api gṛhya-kṛtye / pādau padaṃ na calatas tava pāda-mūlād yāmaḥ kathaṃ vrajam atho karavāma kiṃ vā'.

statements.claim: "Quench the fire that your smiling glance and your sweet songs have lit in our hearts — or else we will be burned up by the pain of missing you, and reach your feet only through our meditation on you."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.34: 'siñcāṅga nas tvad-adharāmṛta-pūrakeṇa hāsāvaloka-kala-gīta-ja-hṛc-chayāgnim / no ced vayaṃ virahajāgny-upayukta-dehā dhyānena yāma padayoḥ padavīṃ sakhe te'.

statements.claim: "What woman in the three worlds, hearing the song of your flute, could keep to the path of the good and not come running? Seeing your face with its smiling eyes and dark curls, your arms that grant fearlessness, your chest that is the home of fortune herself — place your lotus hand upon our heads. You take away the fears of Vraja, the friend of the afflicted."
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.38-40: 'vīkṣyālakāvṛta-mukhaṃ ... hasitāvalokam / dattābhayaṃ ca bhuja-daṇḍa-yugaṃ vilokya vakṣaḥ śriyaika-ramaṇaṃ ca bhavāma dāsyaḥ / kā stry aṅga te kala-padāyata-veṇu-gīta-sammohitārya-caritān na calet tri-lokyām / vyaktaṃ bhavān vraja-bhayārti-haro ... tan no nidhehi kara-paṅkajam ārta-bandho ... kiṅkarīṇām'.

notes: Nearly every clause of Krishna's speech and the gopis' reply maps to SB 10.29.17-41. 'Autumn night' is traditional rasa-lila seasonal framing not stated in the pack passage — flagged as connective narration, not contradicted by the pack.

statements.claim: Across the dark water of the Yamuna the gopis were calling his name, and Krishna listened for a long while before he moved.
statements.evidence: Scene-setting before SB 10.29.42 ('tābhiḥ sametābhir' — with them gathered); the gopis' calling/grieving is the immediately preceding content of 10.29.28-41.

statements.claim: These were the milkmaids of Vrindavan who had left their homes at the sound of his flute and followed him to the river on a full-moon night.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.2-7 (in the adjacent pack): flute song summoning the vraja-striyaḥ on the full-moon night, minds seized, homes abandoned.

statements.claim: Earlier that evening he had hidden from them, to test them, to see whether their devotion could survive his silence.
statements.evidence: The pack's own narrative has Krishna present and speaking throughout the test (SB 10.29.16-27: he welcomed them and told them to return; 10.29.16 'avavadad vadatāṃ śreṣṭho vācaḥ peśair vimohayan' — the best of speakers spoke, charming them with words). He hid neither in silence nor by absence; his vanishing comes only later at 10.29.47. The story conflates the verbal test with the later disappearance.

statements.claim: They had not turned back and gone home; they had only grieved and gone on calling for him, and it was that grief that moved him at last.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.28-41: the gopis, refusing to leave, lament and plead; 10.29.42-46 then shows him relenting and consoling them ('tābhiḥ sametābhir udāra-ceṣṭitaḥ ... priyekṣaṇotphulla-mukhībhir acyutaḥ').

statements.claim: The verses are careful to say he was already self-satisfied, already full, and that nothing he did that night came from any need of his own; yet he smiled a smile of favor and showed them grace.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Krishna, though self-satisfied, smilingly showed them favor and enjoyed himself with them'; SB 10.29.46: 'evaṃ bhagavataḥ kṛṣṇāl labdha-mānā mahātmanaḥ'.

statements.claim: He came down to the cool, sandy bank of the river, into the soft light of the full moon.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.44: 'nadyāḥ pulinam āviśya gopībhir hima-vālukam' — entering the river's sandbank, cool with sand, with the gopis.

statements.claim: The moment they saw him their faces opened like flowers; they sang to him and he sang with them, one voice answering another, a hundred voices braided together.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.42-43: 'priyekṣaṇotphulla-mukhībhir' — faces blossoming at the sight of the beloved; 'upagīyamāna udgāyan vanitā-śata-yūthapaḥ' — sung to, himself singing, leader of a hundred women.

statements.claim: He spread his arms wide and drew them near, and the verses say he embraced them and returned their affection with the light play of his fingertips — laughter, a hand at the fold of a garment.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.45: 'bāhu-prasāra-parirambha-karālakoru nīvī-stanālabhana-narma-nakhāgra-pātaiḥ' — outstretched arms, embraces, touching of garment-knots, play, nail-tips.

statements.claim: The verses record only that it happened, on the bank of the Yamuna, on sand that stayed cool through the night.
statements.evidence: SB 10.29.42-46; 'hima-vālukam' (cool sand) at 10.29.44.

statements.claim: These women, who moments before had believed themselves abandoned, now felt themselves the most blessed women alive — not because they had earned him, but because he had chosen to come back to them.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'the gopis thought themselves the most blessed of women'; SB 10.29.46: 'labdha-mānā' — having obtained his honor/favor.

corrections.original_sentence: Earlier that evening he had hidden from them, to test them, to see whether their devotion could survive his silence.
corrections.suggested: Earlier that evening he had tested them, sending them back with words meant to turn them away, to see whether their devotion could survive his refusal.

notes: One CONTRADICTED: the story says Krishna tested the gopis by hiding in silence, but the pack (10.29.16-27) has him present and testing them verbally; his vanishing belongs to 10.29.47 (next story). Everything else maps to 10.29.42-46.

statements.claim: One moment he was there among them; the next, the gopis turned and he was gone — no word, no warning.
statements.evidence: The disappearance is the established preceding event (SB 10.29.47, prev story DKS_0098); 10.30.1-3 opens with the gopis' frantic search.

statements.claim: They went into the forest like women out of their minds, searching from wood to wood and singing his name aloud.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.3: 'gāyantya uccair amum eva saṃhatā vicikyur unmattaka-vad vanād vanam'.

statements.claim: As they searched they took on his very manner — his walk, his smile, the way he glanced, the sweet way he spoke — until each gopi seemed to carry a little of him.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.1-2: 'gatyānurāga-smita-vibhramekṣitair mano-ramālāpa-vihāra-vibhramaiḥ / gati-smita-prekṣaṇa-bhāṣaṇādiṣu priyāḥ priyasya pratirūḍha-mūrtayaḥ' — in gait, smile, glance and speech they embodied the beloved's form.

statements.claim: They questioned the trees — the ashvattha, the plaksha and the great banyan — asking: have you seen Nanda's son, the one who stole our hearts with his smiles?
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.4: 'dṛṣṭo vaḥ kaccid aśvattha plakṣa nyagrodha no manaḥ'; the question's wording per pack excerpt: 'Have you seen Nanda's son, who stole our hearts with his smiles?'

statements.claim: They turned to the flowering trees — the ashoka, the kurabaka, the champaka, the nagakesara and the punnaga — and to the tulasi plant, which they called the one beloved of Govinda's feet.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.5-6: 'kaccit kurabakāśoka-nāga-punnāga-campakāḥ / kaccit tulasi kalyāṇi govinda-caraṇa-priye'.

statements.claim: They asked the mango, the jackfruit, the kadamba, the bilva, the bakula and the nipa, the jasmine and the creepers that twine up the trunks, which the verses picture throwing their arms around a great tree like a friend embracing a friend.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.7-8: 'mālaty adarśi vaḥ kaccin mallike jāti-yūthike / cūta-priyāla-panasāsana-kovidāra jambv-arka-bilva-bakulāmra-kadamba-nīpāḥ'; 10.30.12: 'pṛcchatemā latā bāhūn apy āśliṣṭā vanaspateḥ'.

statements.claim: They turned on the earth itself and demanded to know what penance it had performed that the mere touch of his feet should make it blossom — whether it was his stride or the touch of his feet.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.9: 'kiṃ te kṛtaṃ kṣiti tapo bata keśavāṅghri-sparśotsavotpulakitāṅga-nahair vibhāsi / apy aṅghri-sambhava urukrama-vikramād vā'.

statements.claim: They asked the doe whether Krishna had come this way — his arm on a beloved's shoulder, a lotus in his hand, the tulasi garland around his neck with bees drunk on its scent, the jasmine garland carrying the perfume of the one he loved — and whether the trees had bowed to him, honored by his loving glance.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.10-11: 'apy eṇa-patny upagataḥ priyayeha ... kāntāṅga-saṅga-kuca-kuṅkuma-rañjitāyāḥ kunda-srajaḥ kula-pater iha vāti gandhaḥ / bāhuṃ priyāṃsa upadhāya gṛhīta-padmo rāmānujas tulasikāli-kulair madāndhaiḥ / anvīyamāna iha vas taravaḥ praṇāmaṃ kiṃ vābhinandati caran praṇayāvalokaiḥ'.

statements.claim: The forest kept its silence; the trees held their branches still, and the gopis went on from tree to tree, calling the question again and again, because asking was the only thing left to do.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric close to the questioning passage (10.30.1-12); the text records no answers from the trees, so the silence is consistent — no factual assertion needing source.

notes: All tree-by-tree questioning maps to SB 10.30.1-12, including the exact tree lists and the doe/earth questions.

statements.claim: Still searching and calling Krishna's name, the gopis began to enact his deeds in the forest, for no audience but the trees and the moon.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.13: 'ity unmatta-vaco gopyaḥ kṛṣṇānveṣaṇa-kātarāḥ' — speaking thus madly, distressed in the search; the enactments follow in 10.30.14-22.

statements.claim: The verses call their words the words of the frantic.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.13: 'unmatta-vacaḥ' — words of the frantic.

statements.claim: One woman played Putana, the demoness who had come to the village disguised as a wet-nurse with poison on her breast to kill the infant Krishna, and another played Krishna and drank at her breast, having drawn out the demon's very life with the milk.
statements.evidence: Enactment: SB 10.30.14: 'kasyācit pūtanāyantyāḥ kṛṣṇāyanty apibat stanam'. The Putana backstory (wet-nurse disguise, poisoned breast, life sucked out with the milk) matches the earlier corpus episode SB 10.6 and is framed in the story as 'the story they had all heard'.

statements.claim: Another took the part of the demon who had come as a wooden cart to crush the sleeping child: she carried off a gopi playing the baby Krishna, who kicked out with a small foot and overturned the cart, the way the real Krishna once had.
statements.evidence: Enactment: SB 10.30.15: 'daityāyitvā jahārānyām eko kṛṣṇārbha-bhāvanām'. The śakaṭāsura backstory (10.7: demon as a cart; baby Krishna struck it with his foot) is prior corpus lore.

statements.claim: Two of them became Krishna and Balarama, and around them other gopis became the cowherd boys, calling to one another the way the herders did at pasture.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.16-17: 'kṛṣṇa-rāmāyite dve tu gopāyantyaś ca kāścana / āhūya dūra-gā yadvat kṛṣṇas tam anuvartatīm'.

statements.claim: One raised her arm high above her head, the way Krishna had raised the hill of Govardhana on a single finger to shelter the village from the storm, and called out: do not fear the wind or the rain; I have made you a shelter.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.18-19: 'kasyāñcit sva-bhujaṃ nyasya calanty āhāparā nanu / mā bhaiṣṭa vāta-varṣābhyāṃ tat-trāṇaṃ vihitaṃ maya'. Govardhana backstory (10.25) is prior corpus lore.

statements.claim: One climbed up onto another and stamped down with her foot, as Krishna had once danced upon the hoods of the serpent Kaliya in the river's poisoned waters.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.20: 'āruhyaikā padākramya śirasy āhāparāṃ nṛpa'. Kaliya episode (10.16-17) is prior corpus lore.

statements.claim: Another pointed into the distance and cried: O cowherds, see the fierce forest fire — the fire Krishna had once swallowed whole to save them.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.21: 'tatraikovāca he gopā dāvāgniṃ paśyatolbaṇam'. The swallowing of the forest fire (10.19) is prior corpus lore.

statements.claim: One slim gopi sat down and let herself be tied with a garland of flowers to a tree, the way the child Krishna had been tied by his mother to the grinding mortar for his mischief, and had slipped free even then.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.22: 'baddhānyayā srajā kācit tanvī tatra ulūkhale' — the slim gopi was tied there at a grinding MORTAR (ulūkhala) with a garland, not to a tree. Krishna's own binding (10.9) was likewise to the mortar. The story's own visual_elements field says 'the tied child and the grinding mortar', so 'to a tree' is an internal inconsistency as well.

statements.claim: Through it all they went on asking the trees and creepers of Vrindavan: have you seen him?
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.23: 'evaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ pṛcchamānā vrṇdāvana-latās tarūn'.

corrections.original_sentence: And one slim gopi sat down and let herself be tied with a garland of flowers to a tree, the way the child Krishna had been tied by his mother to the grinding mortar for his mischief, and had slipped free even then.
corrections.suggested: One slim gopi sat down and let herself be tied with a garland of flowers at a grinding mortar, the way the child Krishna had been tied by his mother to the mortar for his mischief, and had slipped free even then.

notes: One CONTRADICTED: the gopi bound herself at a mortar (SB 10.30.22 'ulūkhale'), not to a tree. All six enactments (Putana, cart, Krishna-Balarama, Govardhana, Kaliya, forest fire) map to SB 10.30.13-22; childhood backstories match earlier corpus episodes (10.6, 10.7, 10.25, 10.16, 10.19, 10.9).

statements.claim: In the soft earth the footprints stopped them; they knew them at once: the marks of Nanda's son.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.24: 'padāni vyaktam etāni nanda-sūnor mahātmanaḥ'.

statements.claim: Beside Krishna's footprints ran another set, smaller and lighter — the steps of one of their own — and where the two went on together the ground was pressed deeper, as though he had carried her.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.26: 'kasyāḥ padāni caitāni yātāyā nanda-sūnunā'; 10.30.30: 'imāny adhika-magnāni padāni vahato vadhūm' — deeper prints of one carrying the bride.

statements.claim: Here flowers had been gathered — picked for her, by him — and here a woman's hair had been dressed by careful hands.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.31-32: 'atra prasūnāvacayaḥ priyārthe preyasā kṛtaḥ / keśa-prasādhanaṃ tv atra kāminyāḥ kāminā kṛtam'.

statements.claim: The gopis called the dust of those footprints blessed: blessed is the dust of Govinda's feet.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.28: 'dhanyā aho amī ālyo govindāṅghry-abja-reṇavaḥ'.

statements.claim: The verses do not say the others were angry; they say they marveled and ached — this woman must have worshiped him as no one else had, for him to single her out; he had taken her aside and kept her to himself in the deep of the forest.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.27: 'anayārādhito nūnaṃ bhagavān harir īśvaraḥ'; 10.30.29: 'tasyā amūni naḥ kṣobhaṃ kurvanty uccaiḥ padāni yat yaikāpahṛtya gopīnām raho bhunkte 'cyutādharam' — her footprints agitate us, for she, taken apart from the gopis, enjoys Acyuta's lips in private.

statements.claim: The verses add that though he is self-delighted and self-satisfied, whole in himself and undivided, he had enjoyed her company all the same.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.33: 'reme tayā cātma-rata ātmārāmo 'py akhaṇḍitaḥ'.

statements.claim: The one he had chosen began to think herself the greatest of all women.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.35: 'sā ca mene tadātmānaṃ variṣṭhaṃ sarva-yoṣitām'.

statements.claim: When she found Krishna waiting in a farther part of the forest, she told him she was tired — that she could not walk — and that he should carry her wherever he chose.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.36: 'tato gatvā vanoddeśaṃ dṛptā keśavam abravīt'; pack excerpt: 'asked Krishna to carry her'; the request's content is implied by 10.30.37 'skandha āruhyatām iti' — climb onto my shoulder.

statements.claim: Krishna answered: Climb onto my shoulder, and I will take you.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.37: 'evam uktaḥ priyām āha skandha āruhyatām iti'.

statements.claim: At the very moment she would have settled onto his shoulder, Krishna was gone — vanished into the air, leaving her with nothing under her hands.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'when he took her on his shoulder he vanished again, and she repented'.

statements.claim: The verses give her cry: O lord, O my beloved, where are you, where are you, mighty-armed one? The forest gave back no answer.
statements.evidence: SB 10.30.38: 'hā nātha ramaṇa preṣṭha kvāsi kvāsi mahā-bhuja'.

statements.claim: She had been lifted to the highest place of all, and she had thought it was her own. Now she stood alone, and understood.
statements.evidence: Interpretive close consistent with pack excerpt ('she repented') and verse 35 (her pride); no separate factual assertion.

notes: All plot points (footprints, deeper prints, flowers, hair-dressing, marveling, pride, request to be carried, second vanishing, cry) map to SB 10.30.24-39.
